entries.title: The interface between this paper's deliverables and the overall research objective
entries.complete_task_relation: Overall objective -> locally solved subtask -> outputs for the next task -> end-to-end conclusions not yet established.
entries.distinction: Application motivation or improved intermediate quantities do not establish system benefits. The series interface in F05 and strategy-family scope in F51 are complementary and need different sufficient checks.
entries.effect_and_pass: Readers may misidentify the local contribution or mistake conditional achievable results for capacity. Clear outputs, external dependencies, and claim scope suffice.
entries.revision_move: State local deliverables, downstream uses, and unfinished interfaces in that order. Narrow scope when needed; do not invent end-to-end validation.

entries.title: Levels of theoretical guarantees and evidence identity
entries.complete_task_relation: Assumptions -> actual theorem -> algorithm-output properties -> experimental observations -> conclusion wording.
entries.distinction: Monotone objectives, stationarity, local optima, and global optima differ; plot agreement is not exact equality. F13/F48 explicitly retain unproved parts, whereas F10/F29/F42/F44 include source wording requiring caution.
entries.effect_and_pass: Incorrect guarantees distort reliability and optimality judgments. State only the established level; a global proof is not always necessary.
entries.revision_move: Separate theorem and numerical observations. Narrow wording to stationarity when that is proved, or identify the additional proof needed for a stronger claim.

entries.title: Which old proofs survive algorithm modifications?
entries.complete_task_relation: Original algorithm and assumptions -> changed constraints, updates, or structure -> retained properties -> broken properties -> revised claim scope.
entries.distinction: Fixed-parameter results do not automatically cover adaptation; solvability does not preserve a closed form; structural zeros may destroy irreducibility.
entries.effect_and_pass: Invalid convergence or complexity claims may be inherited. Verify required invariants or identify an empirical method honestly.
entries.revision_move: Describe the changed step, check proof dependencies, retain valid parts, and prove, test, or narrow statements affected by failed assumptions.

entries.title: Distinguish convergence, feasibility, timeout, and successful-sample statistics
entries.complete_task_relation: Service requirements and resource caps -> feasibility -> stopping event -> output-constraint checks -> success/failure statistics.
entries.distinction: A fixed point may violate service requirements, a budget timeout is not infeasibility, and conditional average iterations do not represent all trials. F19's uncapped feasibility cannot transfer to capped power.
entries.effect_and_pass: Reliability can be overstated or negative-power formulas called executable. Define events and denominators and supply appropriate feasibility evidence.
entries.revision_move: Define success and failure first, then conditional statistics and failure handling. Rewording must not conceal unchecked feasibility.

entries.title: The gap between transformed solving and original-problem recovery
entries.complete_task_relation: Original problem -> preserved sets/objectives -> auxiliary solution -> original-variable recovery -> feasibility -> objective/bound closure.
entries.distinction: Equal optima do not automatically give an original feasible solution; feasible scaling need not preserve optimality; order and auxiliary noise may be mapping inputs. F49 closes bounds with a witness, while F48 limits recovery conditionally.
entries.effect_and_pass: Solver outputs may not support original-system claims. Valid recovery, residuals, and appropriate certificates suffice; explicit suboptimal recovery is acceptable.
entries.revision_move: Add recovery steps and conditions. With numerical evidence only, report recovered objectives and residuals instead of replacing original results with auxiliary results.

entries.title: Distinguish necessary conditions, sufficient constructions, and uniqueness
entries.complete_task_relation: Task constraints -> necessary conditions -> sufficient conditions or construction -> remaining gaps -> alternative optima.
entries.distinction: One implementation is not uniquely necessary; hardware lower bounds and sufficient counts need not give an exact minimum; optimum sum rate can correspond to multiple points.
entries.effect_and_pass: Review can force unnecessary designs or exaggerate minimum resources. Other implementations satisfying the same conditions should pass.
entries.revision_move: State solution conditions before explaining the chosen representative's additional implementation benefit. Keep bounds when the exact minimum remains unknown.

entries.title: Identify comparison policies and certify reference values
entries.complete_task_relation: Compared policy families -> optimization degree -> constraints/information -> reference status -> supported interpretation.
entries.distinction: A relaxed local solution is not a certified bound; binary enumeration is not a continuous global optimum; cancellation baselines include scheduling policies. F25 gives bound logic, while F11/F42 reveal wording risks.
entries.effect_and_pass: A weaker baseline or numerical reference can be mistaken for the strongest competitor. Accurate reference names and scoped conclusions suffice without a global benchmark in every paper.
entries.revision_move: State policy domains, optimization, and certificates. Without certification, use numerical-reference wording and remove unsupported optimum-gap claims.

entries.title: Attribute module gains and identify parameter-scan direction
entries.complete_task_relation: Proposed mechanism -> other fixed factors -> changed module/environment -> performance changes -> supported mechanism explanation.
entries.distinction: Changing design with fixed reality differs from changing reality with fixed design. Shared subchannel allocation better isolates a power module. Simultaneous changes limit causal attribution.
entries.effect_and_pass: Regime or other-module gains may be assigned to the proposed design. Explaining combined comparisons can suffice; ablation is not always mandatory.
entries.revision_move: Identify fixed and varied quantities and baseline roles. Rewrite from existing evidence, narrow causality without isolation, or list needed experiments.

entries.title: Metric units, aggregation, and time scales
entries.complete_task_relation: Required performance -> metric and units -> user/system aggregation -> instantaneous/long-term scale -> actual conclusion.
entries.distinction: Equal diversity order allows constant signal-to-noise gains; realization-level fairness differs from mean fairness; user capacity, bit rate, aggregate values, and per-user optimality are not interchangeable.
entries.effect_and_pass: Correct numbers can support incorrect service judgments. Define metrics precisely and match the claimed scale.
entries.revision_move: Name measurement objects, units, and aggregation before interpretation. Per-block claims need per-block evidence or must become long-term claims.

entries.title: Computation and communication costs must cover actual execution
entries.complete_task_relation: Required data -> acquisition/exchange -> per-step work -> inner/outer counts -> physical latency/net resources -> implementation claim.
entries.distinction: Fewer outer rounds need not mean less work, local updates can need feedback, and virtual quantities need not be locally measurable. Cases address complementary costs, not mandatory exact measurement of every cost.
entries.effect_and_pass: Complexity, distributed, or real-time claims may omit dominant costs. Complete accounting within the claim, or explicit single-stage comparison, suffices.
entries.revision_move: List information and costs in execution order. Without device measurements, report theoretical costs or iterations rather than fabricated latency.

entries.title: Robustness scope, information loss, and service costs
entries.complete_task_relation: Uncertainty/training contamination -> protection or projection -> retained/lost information -> protected metric -> service utility.
entries.distinction: Smaller uncertainty sets need not improve finite-sample behavior; projection may lose energy; switching off service protects others while eliminating utility. These cases have different technical conditions.
entries.effect_and_pass: Protection-only evaluation can hide degeneration or extend set-based guarantees to every distribution. Pair benefits/costs and specify the error domain.
entries.revision_move: Define uncertainty sources and sets before protection/utility relations. List missing paired data rather than inventing tradeoff values.

entries.title: Bridge limits, finite scale, and operating regimes
entries.complete_task_relation: Theoretical limit or small-scale evidence -> parameter regime -> finite-scale deviations -> deployment conditions -> qualified conclusion.
entries.distinction: Equal leading terms are not equal finite values; small-system enumeration does not prove large-system near-optimality; limiting recovery is a check rather than a full proof.
entries.effect_and_pass: Resource laws or guarantees may be reused in unsupported regimes. State regimes and finite evidence or retain asymptotic scope.
entries.revision_move: Separate strict results from finite-scale observations and add evidence for extrapolated intermediate regimes; a smooth curve does not close a theoretical gap.

entries.title: Separate model duality from implementable and computable duality
entries.complete_task_relation: Objects/policy families -> abstract equivalence -> required order/auxiliary quantities -> acquisition/solution conditions -> physical execution.
entries.distinction: Operational existence does not supply an algorithm; minimax under general convex constraints need not represent fixed-noise physical uplink; reciprocity is not implied by mathematical duality.
entries.effect_and_pass: Unknown auxiliaries can be treated as inputs or implementation scope overstated. State duality types and interfaces clearly.
entries.revision_move: Explain transformation objects, inputs, outputs, and conditions; without construction, retain existence-only scope.

entries.title: Organize the proof around relationships that must be closed
entries.complete_task_relation: Final claim -> subtasks -> each input/output -> bridge conditions -> closing evidence -> uncovered scope.
entries.distinction: Section order or simple-to-complex exposition is not necessary; readers must be able to trace how each step supports the final result.
entries.effect_and_pass: Every local derivation may appear without supporting the final claim. Complete prose, figures, or theorem references can suffice without a fixed format.
entries.revision_move: Rewrite transitions around missing bridges. If the bridge itself is unproved, list technical work needed rather than merely adding therefore.
